name: Yukon

flag.description: Three vertical panels of green, white and blue, the white centre wider, with the territorial coat of arms above a wreath of fireweed in the centre.
flag.symbolism: Green stands for the forests, white for the snow and blue for the lakes and rivers; fireweed is the territorial flower.

hook: Yukon runs green, white and blue, with a coat of arms topped by a husky-like malamute on the white; the Northwest Territories have blue on both sides.
trivia: The flag was picked from a territory-wide design competition in 1967 and adopted on 1 March 1968.
The crest of the coat of arms on the flag is a malamute dog standing on a mound of snow.
